I’ve farmed this 4.1 mu in Quzhou for 50 years now. Last year my wheat gave me about 800 jin per mu and the maize about 900 jin per mu. Not bad, but the electricity for pumping water keeps getting more expensive, and at 65 it’s just me now — my back isn’t what it used to be. I have to watch every yuan because my pension is only a few hundred a month and this farm is basically my whole income.

This October I’ll plant wheat around the 10th, same as everyone in the village. I save my own seed — this variety has done fine for years, so why pay for new seed? Before planting I hire the neighbor with the small tractor to rotary till the field. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — 50 jin — and work it into the soil. That’s what I’ve always done. My neighbor Wang tried using less fertilizer last year and his wheat came up shorter than mine, so I’m not risking that. In spring at jointing time, if the wheat looks a little yellow I’ll spread about 15 kg of urea per mu. I irrigate twice for wheat: wintering water and jointing water. Each time the pump runs it costs electricity money, so I don’t do more unless it’s terribly dry. I spray herbicide in spring, and if I see any disease I’ll spray fungicide too. I hire a combine to harvest in early June — at my age I can’t swing a sickle anymore, and there’s no one in the house to help.

The maize has to go in fast, within two or three days of wheat harvest. You miss that window and you lose yield. I buy hybrid maize seed every year — about 2 kg per mu — because saved hybrid seed doesn’t work. I put compound fertilizer in the planting holes, about 40 kg per mu, then topdress with urea when the maize is knee-high. Two irrigations for maize if July and August are dry. I spray herbicide and keep an eye out for corn borers; if I see them I spray insecticide.

Money is tight, so I don’t buy fancy inputs. But I don’t dare cut too much either — if the yield drops, I won’t have enough to get through the year. I’ll be happy if I get about 800 jin of wheat and 900 jin of maize per mu again.
